questions.question: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive in an area.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. You must drive slower when conditions require it, such as on slippery roads or when visibility is poor.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
That action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: That action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Some regulatory signs forbid actions. These signs are white and rectangular with red and black markings. A red circle with a slash on a black symbol means the action is forbidden.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Stop completely and give the right-of-way to others.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Release the gas pedal and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and making a small turn. Check for other traffic before steering back.

questions.question: A learner's permit allows a new driver to drive while supervised by:

options.text: A licensed parent, legal guardian, driving instructor, or an adult who signed for financial responsibility.
Any licensed driver.
A driving instructor only.
Any driver over age 21.

questions.correctAnswerText: A licensed parent, legal guardian, driving instructor, or an adult who signed for financial responsibility.
questions.explanation: With a learner's permit, you may only practice driving with a driving instructor, parent, or legal guardian. A responsible licensed adult who signed for financial responsibility may also supervise.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is going up or down at a railroad crossing:

options.text: If a train is not close.
If your vehicle can do so without hitting the gate.
If you look both ways first.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Stops distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to surprises.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between your vehicle and others gives you enough time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Drive to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Move slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Move slowly while staying on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or siren, move as far right as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: You do not need as much following distance behind a motorcycle as behind a car.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. You should stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to maneuver in an emergency.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Apply your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: To slow down on a slippery road, first release the gas pedal. If you need to slow more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space when you need to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially right after it rains. When it rains, water mixes with oil and dirt on the road. Slow down in heavy rain, around standing water, or in slush to keep your tires from sliding.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always let pedestrians cross, even if they are breaking the law.
Only give right-of-way when the pedestrian is following the law.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let pedestrians cross, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and let them cross, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
You should change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is always a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let other cars pass.
May create danger for other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create danger for other drivers.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. If cars are backing up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a crossbuck sign. You should:

options.text: Approach with great care and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Lower your radio volume to listen for a train.
Only go forward if a flagger signals you to do so.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with great care. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow all their instructions.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on that road. The posted speed is for perfect conditions. You must go slower when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always demand the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not have time to stop.

questions.question: Drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes conditions less than ideal.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes conditions less than ideal.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions bad. You can get a ticket for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at the speed limit.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Always drives at the same speed.
Only drives in places they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches for what other drivers do and expects problems to happen.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so they can complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass if it is safe and you will not meet oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make unsafe passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a sharp curve. The arrow shows the direction of the curve. Multiple signs like this may appear throughout the curve.

questions.question: What driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better traction.
Leave the highways as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow and ice. Reducing your speed and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.
